summary: Iter 383 — Verified the two-part chat refactor: (a) createChatWebSocket now exposes .send() and .readyState; (b) ~200-line MessageBubble JSX extracted into /app/frontend/src/components/chat/MessageBubble.js. Frontend smoke + single-user e2e flows on /chat all PASS as admin@meetflow.com: conversation list renders (57 convs, no white screen), opening a conversation shows existing messages with timestamps + (bearbeitet) + read-receipt checkmarks, new message via Enter appears in bubble list, EDIT via data-testid 'msg-edit-{id}' updates IMMEDIATELY with '(bearbeitet)' label, REACTION via 👍 emoji increments counter and renders pill (👍 1), DELETE via data-testid 'msg-delete-{id}' removes bubble IMMEDIATELY (optimistic update from iter 382 still intact). Hover-revealed action toolbar from MessageBubble.js works correctly. The MessageBubble extraction is BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING — no regressions detected for text, edit, reaction, delete, sender-name, timestamp, (bearbeitet), read-receipt-checkmark rendering. BLOCKED: the 2-user typing-indicator and read-receipt WS-push tests could not be executed because the underlying WebSocket endpoint wss://.../api/ws/chat/user_<id> fails to connect in the preview env ('WebSocket is closed before the connection is established' — observed 5× per page load, pre-existing issue from iter 382). The new .send() and .readyState code is correct by inspection (lines 136-148 of chatWebSocket.js), but at runtime ws.readyState never reaches OPEN, so .send() correctly returns false and no typing/read frames are emitted. Special-type bubbles (GIF / voice / file / call) were not present in the test conversations so their render paths were verified by code review only — the MessageBubble.js branches for type==='gif'/'voice'/'call'/'file'/'bot'/'auto-reply' are all present and unchanged.

integration_issues.issue: wss://video-meet-pro.preview.emergentagent.com/api/ws/chat/user_<id> repeatedly fails with 'WebSocket is closed before the connection is established.' (5 attempts seen on every chat page load). Because the socket never reaches readyState===OPEN, the newly-added handle.send() always returns false and no typing/read frames are transmitted. Single-user chat works (edit/delete are optimistic, send goes over REST) so users don't see breakage, but cross-user real-time features (typing indicator, read receipts, message-deleted/message-edited push to other tabs) silently no-op. This is a backend/ingress issue, NOT introduced by the iter 383 change — the iter 383 .send() addition itself is correct code.

action_items: Investigate why wss://.../api/ws/chat/<user_id> closes before connection is established in the preview env — check backend WS endpoint handler exists, ingress allows the Upgrade header on /api/ws/chat/*, and the JWT/cookie is forwarded. Without this, the iter 383 .send() fix cannot deliver typing-indicator / read-receipt frames between users.

Optional: in createChatWebSocket onclose handler, if ws.readyState transitioned 0→3 within < ~500 ms (connect failed before open), back off ONCE quickly then double the delay — currently every failed connect bumps 'attempt' so backoff goes 1s/2s/4s/8s which is fine, but the 5-times-per-page-load noise in the preview console suggests a logging gate could help observability.
critical_code_review_comments: ChatPage.js is now 1255 lines — still ~80 % above the 700-line guideline. Continue the extraction pattern that iter 383 started: pull ChatSidebar (conversation list + filters + new-chat dialog) and MessageInput (composer + file upload + GIF + voice) into separate files; the orchestrator should end up < 600 lines.

MessageBubble.js (line 9) reads API_URL = process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL at module-eval time. That is fine, but the file should also defensively handle the case where it is undefined (e.g. throw at module load) so a misconfigured env fails fast rather than producing the broken `undefined/uploads/...` URLs that VoicePlayer would silently mount.

createChatWebSocket.send() (line 144-148) is correct, but consider also forwarding `bufferedAmount` so future code can implement back-pressure if typing-indicator frames burst — not critical, just future-proofing.

MessageBubble.js receives 19 props — consider grouping the callbacks ({ onEdit, onDelete, onReact, onReply, onThread, onCall, onJoin }) into a single `actions` prop to improve readability and make the component easier to mock in storybook/tests.

deleteMessage(), saveEdit(), toggleReaction() in ChatPage.js all swallow errors with `catch { toast.error('Fehler') }` and lose the server detail. Surface response?.data?.detail like deleteConversation() does so production failures stay diagnosable.

success_rate.frontend: single-user flows: 100% PASS (render, send, edit-optimistic, reaction, delete-optimistic, MessageBubble integration); cross-user WS flows: NOT TESTED (WS endpoint down in preview env)

seed_data_creation: Sent one transient message 'T1 iter383 testmsg' in 'Test Group Remove' conversation; edited to 'T1 iter383 EDITED' (+ 👍 reaction) and then deleted in the same run, so no residual server state remains.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 383 refactor (MessageBubble extraction + WS handle .send/.readyState) is functionally verified for single-user flows. The 2-user typing-indicator / read-receipt e2e cannot be tested in this preview env until the wss://.../api/ws/chat/<user_id> endpoint is fixed (5× 'WebSocket is closed before the connection is established' per page load — same warning observed in iter 382). To unblock cross-user testing: either fix the WS endpoint or create a small unit test that mocks WebSocket and asserts handle.send() returns true when readyState===1 and false otherwise. Useful testids: conv-conv_<id> (sidebar), msg-msg_<id> (bubble — regex /^msg-msg_[a-z0-9]+$/ to exclude the read-receipt span which has data-testid='msg-msg_<id>-read-receipt'), msg-edit-{id} / msg-delete-{id} / msg-edit-input-{id} / msg-edit-save-{id} / msg-edit-cancel-{id}, button[title='Reaktion'] inside the bubble (no testid). Input: input[placeholder*='Nachricht']. The bubble action toolbar is hidden by default and revealed on parent .group hover — always page.hover(bubble) before clicking edit/delete/reaction.
rca of the issue: The iter 383 .send/.readyState addition was correct: previously the createChatWebSocket return value only exposed { close }, so callers in ChatPage.js doing wsRef.current?.send(...) and wsRef.current?.readyState === 1 were silently no-op'ing (undefined method / undefined comparison always false). With the fix, the code path is now LIVE — but it cannot be observed in production because the underlying wss endpoint never reaches OPEN in the preview env. Recommended fix order: (1) fix the WS endpoint upstream so readyState reaches OPEN; (2) then re-run a 2-user test with admin@meetflow.com and a second member to verify typing-indicator '... schreibt' appears in user B's window when user A types, and the double-check (gelesen) appears in user A's bubble when user B opens the chat.
